title: Feasible Recipe Dependency Closure
prompt:
Implement `find_feasible_recipes(recipes, supplies) -> list[str]`. `recipes` is an insertion-ordered mapping from a recipe name to an iterable of required ingredient names. `supplies` is a collection of available raw ingredient names. Recipe names and supply names are distinct. Requirement names are logical dependencies, so a duplicate requirement within one recipe has no additional effect.

A recipe is feasible when every one of its requirements is either in `supplies` or is another feasible recipe. Preparing a feasible recipe does not consume any ingredient. Requirements that are neither supplied nor named by a recipe block that recipe. Cyclic recipe dependencies are not feasible unless every dependency in the cycle is already a raw supply, which this contract excludes. Return every feasible recipe name in the original `recipes` insertion order. Do not mutate either input.

Build a reverse dependency graph and propagate newly feasible recipes through it. Avoid repeatedly scanning every unresolved recipe after each discovery.

example.reasoning: The supplied flour and water make dough feasible, which in turn unlocks flatbread.
